messages:
emma: Quick pass from the design review — three small but important things around expiry visibility, copy after create, and clipboard fallbacks. Wanted to capture before I forget.
neil: Go for it. I can triage front-end work once we settle copy and ARIA behavior.
sara: Saw a couple accessibility failures in the a11y audit related to expiry pills and masked secret interactions. Happy to help.
tom: Also want to avoid scaring users with the wrong tone when a key is disabled vs permanently deleted.
emma: 1) Expiry visibility: add a subtle pill next to key name reading e.g. "Expires in 14 days" or "No expiry". Use humanized relative text but include title attr with ISO timestamp. Important: do not put the pill in the tab order (not actionable) but ensure screen readers announce it as part of the row: aria-label on the row should include expiry text.
neil: Implementation note: we'll receive expiry_ts and can render relative time. Use Intl.RelativeTimeFormat where available and fallback to a localized date string.
sara: For a11y: do not make the pill clickable. Instead ensure the row has aria-describedby pointing to an offscreen element that concatenates status+expiry so screen readers get: "Key name, active, expires in 14 days". That avoids surprising keyboard focus.
tom: 2) Copy/Download flow after key creation: don't auto-download. Show a success drawer with masked secret, Copy and Download buttons. Copy should call navigator.clipboard.writeText on explicit user action and announce "Secret copied to clipboard" via an aria-live polite container. If clipboard.writeText throws or is blocked, surface inline fallback text: "Copy blocked — press Ctrl+C / Cmd+C or use Download" and keep that linked via aria-describedby.
emma: Add an unobtrusive banner in the drawer: "This secret is shown once. Store it now." with a small icon. Use neutral-warning color for emphasis, not red.
neil: Also add a visible masked preview like "••••••••xYz" with a Show button. When user reveals the secret, move focus to the secret container and announce "Secret revealed. It will not be shown again." via aria-live. The Show button should toggle masked/visible and be keyboard operable.
sara: Motion accessibility: respect prefers-reduced-motion. If user prefers reduced motion, the drawer should appear instantly and focus should be moved synchronously. Otherwise, delay moving focus until animation completes to avoid race conditions with screen readers.
tom: 3) Tone and banner colors: soft-delete/disable flows should use a cautionary amber/yellow token and copy that emphasizes recoverability: "Disable key — can be restored within 30 days." Reserve red only for truly permanent deletion and expiry screens.
emma: Small copy proposals: Modal confirm: header "Disable key". Body: "This removes the key from active use. You can restore it within 30 days. After that it will be permanently deleted." Primary button: "Disable key" (destructive). Undo toast: "Key disabled — Undo" (10s, dismissible, shown only if user has restore perms).
neil: Backend gating: frontend should only render Undo affordance when API indicates user.has_permission.restore === true. If the delete call succeeds but user lacks restore perm, show toast without Undo and link to permission docs.
sara: Also callout for screen reader users: when disabling many keys, the summary toast should announce counts via aria-live: "5 keys disabled, 2 failed" and provide a keyboard-focusable "View details" that opens a side panel. Trap focus in the panel and ensure Escape closes it and returns focus to the bulk action checkbox.
tom: Edge-cases: rotating a key while it's in a transient disabled state should be disabled in UI with tooltip "Enable to rotate". Also ensure audit-log entries include scope and actor.
emma: Action items I will own: 1) update modal and toast copy per above; 2) mock up the expiry pill + offscreen ARIA pattern; 3) annotate create drawer with explicit Copy/Download behavior and fallback copy; 4) recommend color token changes for amber vs red.
neil: I'll implement the expiry pill rendering, masked secret preview, copy fallback UI, and Undo gating.
sara: I'll write the screen-reader narration examples and run the a11y regression once patches land.
tom: I'll update the security docs to mention the restore permission behavior and audit logging format.
emma: Thanks all — I'll attach annotated mocks and a tiny spec PR. :sparkles:
